_meta.description: R4 Stage-3 ROUND-3 performance baseline. Round 3 is a VERIFICATION round: the rev3 split-V architecture was implemented and precision-verified in Stage 2 but had never been timed -- every number in DESIGN.md section 12.4 was a model estimate. This file records the FIRST measurements of rev3, taken in one session against the pre-rev3 baseline.
_meta.data_source: same-session A/B, cann-bench run_evaluation.sh -> msprof kernel_details.csv (warmup=3 repeat=5, median of per-step Duration sums). Pass order base1 -> cand -> base2, so base2-vs-base1 is an identical-code drift control. NO Python/torch timing anywhere; JIT compile cost is disclosed separately and is excluded from every figure below.
_meta.programming_mode: Developer (pure Vector) + Ascend-specific T.tile.topk hybrid; pass_configs = R4_PASS_CONFIGS incl. tl.ascend_memory_planning

dispatch.note: derived at runtime by the delivered host function _r4_split_plan(); S_cap = CUBE_CORE_NUM // b_num. Matches DESIGN.md section 13.4 exactly.

non_split_12_verification.requirement: the 12 non-split cases run BYTE-IDENTICAL device code, so they must come out at exactly 1.000x inside the drift band; anything outside it would mean unexpected coupling and must be explained

structural_proof.jit_cache_keys_shared: prewarm_base_warm.json: the BASE arm found only 2 of 72 specializations cold, and both are K1 for cases 12/17 -- shapes the CAND arm never compiles as K1 because they take the split path. Every other entry hit the SAME cache directory as the candidate => identical loaded binaries.
structural_proof.launch_sequence_identical: ksplit_base1/base2 vs ksplit_cand: all 12 non-split cases report 2 main_kernel launches with Block Num [b_num, b_num] in BOTH arms (anomaly_rows=0/144 steps)
structural_proof.conclusion: no code-level coupling mechanism exists; the residual is measurement-level and is the same size as the identical-code control

model_verification_12_4.note: DESIGN.md section 12.4 predictions were model estimates only. This is the first measurement of them.

a_launch.E3_model_residual_verdict: INCONSISTENT (8 of 24 residuals negative) -- section 12.2's F(256)=21.63 us/row was calibrated on the single-kernel K1 and does not transfer to K1B; reported as evidence, not used
a_launch.conclusion_us: < 1.540 (E1 min K2gB Duration; K2gB still does nonzero fold work); conservative planning value <= 3.100 us = 38.8% of the shipped default

guard_relaxation.saturation: the split set saturates at 8 cases for any a_launch <= 2.74 us; the other 10 non-split cases are blocked STRUCTURALLY (S<2 or n_blk_full<2), not by the cost guard
guard_relaxation.probe_caveat: no CannBenchCacheClean kernel in this probe (the harness launches one per step), so absolute us may read slightly optimistic; both arms identical => ratio unaffected
guard_relaxation.recommendation: REPORTED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. Changing _SPLIT_A_LAUNCH_US needs Orchestrator approval AND a same-change update of 4 hardcoded expect_use_split fields in the test tables.

case8_k128_bv2048.question: U3/V-S8: the K_MAX=128,BV=2048 specialization was correctness-proven in Stage 2 but its benefit was never measured
case8_k128_bv2048.verdict: KEEP. Both tasks gain far more than the 3% threshold, so the pre-authorised retreat (adding `and K_MAX == 256` to the guard) is NOT needed and was NOT used. DESIGN.md section 12.4 warning 3 predicted case8's 1.57x/1.87x was OPTIMISTIC because of R-F128; measurement shows the opposite -- mask matches the prediction and fused EXCEEDS it.

block_num_runtime.gate: ksplit_fine.py asserts per step (i) row count == _r4_split_plan-derived launch count, (ii) Block Num sequence == expected, (iii) sum == expected sum, (iv) theorem P2: every split-PARALLEL kernel Block Num <= cube_core_num
block_num_runtime.theorem_p2_runtime: PASS on all 6 CSVs; the tightest point is case7 K1A/K2gA with Block Num == 20 == cube_core_num (exactly one full wave)

cann_bench_end_to_end.source: the cand pass of the A/B IS the DESIGN.md section 11.4 step-11 end-to-end run: cann_performance_eval_20261011_150737 (fused) + _150934 (mask), plus their paired cann_correctness_eval_20261011_150635 / _150836

gates_report.t_hw_rationale: DESIGN.md section 15.3.2: not re-derived. The only ops/elem change is +S cross-split merges, worth +0.15% on case7 -- far inside GATE 1's tolerance. GATE 1 re-ran and reproduced the published values exactly.

roofline_attainment.convention: attain% = 100 * t_hw_us / elapsed_us, same published t_hw for both arms

two_pass_gm_read_caveat.statement: DESIGN.md section 15.3.2 requires this to be stated: the rev3 split path reads `logits` from GM TWICE (K1A for the Sort side, K1B for the softmax side) while the published t_hw charges it ONCE (hap_lib unique-bytes / no-reload-factor convention). Attainment of a SPLIT case is therefore not strictly like-for-like with a CURRENT case.
two_pass_gm_read_caveat.fused: 0/6 split cases affected: 2*t_read stays below t_vector everywhere, so the published floor is unchanged and every case remains vector-bound.
two_pass_gm_read_caveat.mask: 3/6 split cases affected (7, 12, 17): charging the reload makes 2*t_read exceed t_vector, t_hw rises x1.87-1.88 (case7 1.3464->2.5345, case12 1.1676->2.1847, case17 5.3964->10.1587 us) and the attribution flips to READ-bound. Attainment under that口径 would be case7 0.779->1.466%, case12 1.579->2.955%, case17 1.679->3.162%.
two_pass_gm_read_caveat.why_mask_differs: the mask task's arithmetic intensity is only ~2.57 ops/byte, already BELOW the 910b2 ridge point of 3.125 (GATE 4), with a vec/read margin as thin as 1.062x; the fused task is ~11.3 ops/byte (3.6x the ridge) so a doubled read cannot flip it.

jit_compile_cost_DISCLOSED_SEPARATELY.statement: Hard constraint 7: JIT compile time is NOT part of any performance number above. Every figure comes from msprof device Duration. This block is the separate disclosure.

cand_arm.note: all 21 cold compiles are FROZEN kernels (K1/K2g/K2m) that the shared cache had never seen for those shapes; every one of the 4 NEW rev3 split kernels was already warm from Stage 2 (0.02-0.13 s)

base_arm.note: only 2 of 72 cold -- K1 for cases 12 and 17, the two shapes the CAND arm compiles as K1A/K1B instead. This is direct evidence that the frozen kernels share JIT cache keys across both arms.

new_rev3_specializations.measured_against: a FRESH empty TILELANG_CACHE_DIR (/tmp/opencode/r4_tl_cache_r3cold), so this is what a first-ever run on a cold machine pays for the rev3 split kernels

ab_eval_wall_clock_s.note: fused, mask. The candidate arm is NOT slower wall-clock than the baseline arm because both were cache-warm.
